headline: Supreme Court Adopts ‘Victim-Survivor’ in Sexual-Violence Cases
seoTitle: Supreme Court Adopts ‘Victim-Survivor’ Term | FMB News
seoDescription: The Philippine Supreme Court has adopted “victim-survivor” for people who have endured sexual violence, emphasizing both harm and continuing dignity.
deck: The Court said the terminology recognizes the harm suffered while affirming the agency, resilience and continuing dignity of people who survive sexual violence.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Supreme Court has adopted the term “victim-survivor” when referring to people who have endured sexual violence, explaining that the wording recognizes both the harm inflicted and the continuing agency, resilience and dignity of survivors.

The Third Division made the clarification in G.R. No. 271812, a decision promulgated on February 24, 2026 and made public in September. The ruling affirmed a man’s conviction for raping a minor who was the daughter of his common-law partner.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Court upheld the conviction for rape through force or intimidation and imposed reclusion perpetua. It ordered the accused to pay ₱150,000 each in civil indemnity, moral damages and exemplary damages, for a total of ₱450,000, with legal interest from the finality of the decision.

The ruling deleted the phrase “without eligibility for parole” from the penalty. Although the evidence established the survivor’s minority and the accused’s parental relationship, the Court said both circumstances could not be used together to qualify the offense because only minority was alleged in the charging information.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The terminology signals how the judiciary intends to describe people subjected to sexual violence in its decisions. It acknowledges victimization without defining a person only by the violence committed against them.

The judgment also reiterates that a credible survivor’s testimony may be sufficient for conviction and that delayed disclosure does not by itself undermine credibility, particularly when threats, fear or the offender’s moral ascendancy are present.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The Court directed the Department of Social Welfare and Development, through the trial court, to refer the victim-survivor to an appropriate rape crisis center. Available assistance may include psychological counseling, medical and medico-legal services, privacy and safety measures, family support and recovery programs.

Future Supreme Court decisions will show how consistently the terminology is applied across sexual-violence cases and whether lower courts and justice agencies adopt the same wording in their own records and public communications.

verificationNotes: The Supreme Court E-Library decision directly states that “victim-survivor” will replace the conventional term “victim” for people who have endured sexual violence.
The decision confirms the February 24, 2026 promulgation date, the conviction, reclusion perpetua, ₱450,000 total damages and the DSWD referral directive.
GMA News independently corroborates the terminology and disposition and reports that the decision was made public in September 2026.
The report withholds all names and identifying circumstances protected by the Court and does not reproduce unnecessary graphic details.
The photograph is an archival institutional image, not a documentary image of the case. Wikimedia Commons identifies Mike Gonzalez as the creator and CC BY-SA 3.0/GFDL as the available licenses.
